subject: Hardware
title: Computer Organization & Design
subtitle: The Hardware/Software Interface
author: David A. Patterson & John L. Hennessy

pages.title: Overview: Abstraction & Technology
bulletPoints: Computer generations: From vacuum tubes and discrete transistors to VLSI and multi-core SoCs.
The Great Architecture Ideas: Abstraction, Moore's law, common-case acceleration, pipelining, and parallelism.
Performance metrics: Latency (execution time) vs throughput (bandwidth), MIPS, FLOPS, and CPU clock cycles.
Classic CPU performance equation: CPU Time = Instruction Count × CPI × Clock Cycle Time.

pages.title: Instructions: Language of the Computer
bulletPoints: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) as the fundamental hardware/software abstraction boundary.
RISC vs CISC principles: Fixed-width 32-bit instructions vs variable-length microcoded encodings.
Registers, immediate operands, and data transfer instructions (Load/Store architecture).
Logical operations, bitwise manipulation, shifts (logical vs arithmetic), and conditional branch evaluation.

pages.title: Arithmetic for Computers
bulletPoints: Signed and unsigned representations, Two's complement arithmetic, and sign extension.
High-speed binary addition: Carry-Ripple Adder vs Carry-Lookahead Adder (CLA) hierarchy.
Sequential and Booth's multiplication algorithms, Wallace tree multipliers, and array dividers.
IEEE 754 Floating-Point Standard: Sign, exponent bias, normalized mantissa, denormals, NaNs, and infinities.

pages.title: The Processor: Datapath & Control
bulletPoints: Single-cycle datapath design: Program counter (PC), instruction memory, register file, ALU, and data memory.
Control unit synthesis: Generating control signals (RegWrite, ALUSrc, MemtoReg, Branch) from opcodes and funct fields.
Critical path timing analysis: Why single-cycle implementations are constrained by the slowest instruction (Load Word).
Multi-cycle execution concepts: Breaking instruction latency into balanced clock stages.

pages.title: Pipelining Architecture & Throughput
bulletPoints: The classic 5-stage RISC pipeline: IF (Fetch), ID (Decode), EX (Execute), MEM (Memory), and WB (Writeback).
Pipeline throughput scaling: Speedup = Pipeline Depth / (1 + Pipeline Stall Cycles).
Pipeline registers: Storing intermediate results, control signals, and destination register indices between clock cycles.
Balanced stage latency: Resolving pipeline clock frequency limitations caused by ALU or cache memory access.

pages.title: Pipeline Hazards & Forwarding
bulletPoints: Structural hazards: Resolving memory port contention using separate Harvard L1 I-cache and D-cache.
Data hazards: Read-After-Write (RAW) dependencies and pipeline stalling (bubbles).
Hardware forwarding (bypassing): Routing ALU output directly from EX/MEM and MEM/WB registers back to ALU inputs.
Load-use data hazards: Why a 1-cycle stall is architecturally unavoidable before forwarding can supply loaded data.

pages.title: Branch Hazards & Prediction
bulletPoints: Control hazards: Penalty of delayed branch resolution in deep execution pipelines.
Static branch prediction: Branch-Taken vs Branch-Not-Taken assumptions and compiler delayed branching.
Dynamic 1-bit and 2-bit saturating counter branch prediction schemes.
Branch Target Buffers (BTB), correlation (two-level adaptive) predictors, and modern TAGE predictor engines.

pages.title: Memory Hierarchy & Locality
bulletPoints: The Memory Wall: Widening performance gap between processor clock frequencies and DRAM access latencies.
Principle of Temporal Locality: If a memory location is referenced, it will likely be referenced again soon.
Principle of Spatial Locality: Memory locations near recently referenced addresses are likely to be accessed next.
Hierarchy levels: CPU registers (sub-nanosecond) -> L1 -> L2 -> L3 caches -> Main DRAM -> NVMe SSDs.

pages.title: Cache Organization & Placement
bulletPoints: Direct-mapped caches: Mapping memory addresses to cache lines using Tag, Index, and Block Offset fields.
Set-associative caches: Reducing conflict misses through N-way set organization.
Fully associative caches: Highest hit rate with parallel content-addressable memory (CAM) tag matching.
Cache block replacement policies: Least Recently Used (LRU), pseudo-LRU, FIFO, and Random eviction.

pages.title: Cache Performance & Optimization
bulletPoints: Average Memory Access Time: AMAT = Hit Time + (Miss Rate × Miss Penalty).
The 3 C's of Cache Misses: Compulsory (cold), Capacity (cache size limits), and Conflict (collision) misses.
Multi-level cache design: Fast L1 for hit time, large inclusive/exclusive L2/L3 for miss rate reduction.
Write policies: Write-Through with write buffers vs Write-Back with dirty bits; Write-Allocate vs No-Write-Allocate.

pages.title: Virtual Memory & Address Translation
bulletPoints: Virtual address space: Providing process memory isolation, protection, and boundless virtual illusion.
Page tables: Mapping virtual page numbers (VPN) to physical frame numbers (PFN) with protection flags.
Multi-level hierarchical page tables: Compacting sparse address space representation.
Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB): High-speed hardware cache for virtual-to-physical address mappings.

pages.title: TLB Misses & Page Fault Handling
bulletPoints: Hardware-managed TLB vs software-managed TLB traps and page table walk latency.
Page faults: Trapping to the operating system kernel when a requested page is not present in physical RAM.
Swap space management: Bringing page frames from NVMe disk and updating page table entries.
Virtual memory aliasing, page colouring, and virtually indexed physically tagged (VIPT) caches.

pages.title: Instruction-Level Parallelism (ILP)
bulletPoints: Overcoming scalar pipeline limits: Superscalar architectures fetching and executing multiple instructions per cycle.
Static multiple issue: Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) architectures and compiler scheduling.
Dynamic multiple issue: Hardware scheduling of independent instructions into execution reservation stations.
True dependencies vs false dependencies: Name dependencies (Anti-dependence WAR, Output dependence WAW).

pages.title: Out-of-Order Execution & Tomasulo's Algorithm
bulletPoints: Tomasulo's dynamic scheduling algorithm: Distributing reservation stations across functional execution units.
Common Data Bus (CDB): Broadcasting execution results directly to waiting reservation stations and register files.
Register Renaming: Eliminating WAR and WAW hazards by mapping architectural registers to physical rename registers.
Reorder Buffer (ROB): Guaranteeing in-order instruction retirement and precise interrupt handling.

pages.title: Parallel Processors & Multicores
bulletPoints: Flynn's Classical Taxonomy: SISD, SIMD, MISD, and MIMD computational models.
Shared-memory multiprocessors (SMP) vs distributed-memory clusters (NUMA architectures).
Interconnection networks: Crossbars, 2D mesh, torus, and ring topologies.
Amdahl's Law and Gustafson's Law: Realistic limits on speedup as processing cores scale.

pages.title: Cache Coherence & Memory Consistency
bulletPoints: The cache coherence problem in multi-core systems: Inconsistent cached values across CPU cores.
Snooping bus protocols: The MSI, MESI, and MOESI state transition automata.
Directory-based cache coherence: Scalable coherence tracking for large NUMA architectures.
Memory consistency models: Strict consistency, sequential consistency, relaxed consistency, and memory fences.

pages.title: Vector Architecture & SIMD
bulletPoints: Vector registers, vector length registers, and vector stride control.
SIMD extensions in modern processors: Intel AVX-512, ARM Neon, and RISC-V Vector (RVV).
Loop vectorization: Transforming scalar loops into parallel vector arithmetic operations.
Vector gather/scatter instructions and masked execution for conditional vector lanes.

pages.title: Graphics Processing Units (GPUs)
bulletPoints: Heterogeneous computing: High-throughput massively parallel architectures vs low-latency CPU cores.
Single Instruction, Multiple Threads (SIMT) execution model and warp/wavefront scheduling.
GPU memory hierarchy: Global device memory, shared memory scratchpads, constant caches, and register files.
Divergent branch execution in SIMT: Serialization and masked inactive thread execution.

pages.title: Storage & Input/Output Systems
bulletPoints: Bus protocols: Synchronous vs asynchronous buses, PCIe lanes, and packet-based switched fabrics.
Direct Memory Access (DMA): Relieving the CPU from high-volume data block transfers.
Interrupt handling: Polling vs vectored interrupts, interrupt service routines, and priority levels.
RAID architectures: Striping (RAID 0), Mirroring (RAID 1), Distributed Parity (RAID 5/6).

pages.title: Domain-Specific Architectures & Accelerators
bulletPoints: The end of Dennard scaling and slowdown of Moore's Law: The rise of specialized hardware accelerators.
Google Tensor Processing Unit (TPU): Systolic array architectures for matrix multiplication.
Quantization in deep learning: FP32 to FP16, Bfloat16, and INT8 inference pipelines.
Zero-copy DMA and unified memory architectures in modern mobile and datacenter silicon.

pages.title: Energy, Power & Thermal Constraints
bulletPoints: Dynamic power equation: P_dynamic = 1/2 × Capacitance × Voltage^2 × Frequency.
Static leakage power: Sub-threshold leakage currents in deep sub-micron process nodes.
Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) and power gating techniques.
Dark Silicon phenomenon: Inability to power all silicon areas simultaneously under thermal design power (TDP).

pages.title: Fault Tolerance & Dependability
bulletPoints: Metrics: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), and Availability.
Error detection and correction: Parity bits, Hamming codes (SECDED), and Cyclic Redundancy Checks (CRC).
Soft errors caused by alpha particles and cosmic rays in dense SRAM cache cells.
Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) and lockstep execution in mission-critical aerospace hardware.

pages.title: Modern SoC Integration & Interconnects
bulletPoints: System-on-Chip (SoC) convergence: Integrating CPU, GPU, NPU, ISP, and memory controllers on single dies.
Network-on-Chip (NoC): Packet-routed on-chip communications replacing shared hierarchical buses.
2.5D and 3D packaging technologies: Silicon interposers, TSVs (Through-Silicon Vias), and chiplet modularity.
High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM): Stacking DRAM dies with thousands of wide interface interconnects.

pages.title: Security at the Hardware Level
bulletPoints: Microarchitectural side-channel attacks: Meltdown, Spectre, and transient execution vulnerabilities.
Cache timing attacks: Measuring cache hit vs miss latency to infer secret cryptographic keys.
Hardware Root of Trust: Secure enclaves, TPMs, signed bootloaders, and cryptographic coprocessors.
Memory protection: Pointer authentication codes (PAC), shadow call stacks, and memory tagging.

pages.title: Future Directions in Computer Architecture
bulletPoints: Neuromorphic computing: Spiking neural networks mimicking biological synaptic structures.
Quantum computing interfaces: Cryogenic CMOS controllers interfacing with superconducting qubits.
Near-memory computing and processing-in-memory (PIM) to eliminate the Von Neumann memory bottleneck.
Open-source silicon revolution: The global impact and extensible future of RISC-V.
